name: Electric chin-reducing mask

card.summary: A strap or mask worn under the chin that delivers electrical muscle stimulation (and sometimes vibration or light) and is marketed to tone the jaw and neck for a firmer-looking chin line.
card.aka: Electric Mask double-chin strap; EMS jowl mask
card.note: Not for people with pacemakers or implanted devices; some users find it painful.

quick.overview:
Electric chin-reducing masks are straps or silicone masks that wrap the jaw and send electrical pulses to muscles under the chin and along the jaw. They are marketed to firm the area and make the jawline look more defined.

Sellers claim lifting and firming; independent clinical trials of these products were not found. One reporter using a similar facial EMS mask reported a more defined chin after two weeks, which is anecdotal.
quick.how: The device is fitted to the face or under the chin, with moistened contact where required, and run in short automatic sessions, typically about ten minutes in the case of one popular facial EMS mask.
quick.risks: Vendors advise people with pacemakers or implanted electronics or who are pregnant to check with a clinician first. Users report discomfort at higher intensities.

lead: The electric chin-reducing mask is a strap or mask that uses electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) to contract muscles around the chin and jaw, sold as a way to tone away the look of a double chin.

Related products include YA-MAN's Medi Lift, a silicone mask with EMS controllers on the cheeks, a "training" mode to lift and a "release" mode to relax clenched muscles, in ten-minute automatic sessions.[1] Some strap products add vibration, LED light or micro-current, with vendors claiming firming effects.
No independent clinical trials of these chin masks were located; descriptions come from manufacturers and reviewers.

chain: Device delivers EMS to chin muscles
angle.text: Users wear the strap or mask in short sessions hoping for a tighter chin line. Results reported are anecdotal.

paras: Types include silicone masks with cheek controllers, straps with a built-in controller, and pad-based jowl masks.[1]

A SoraNews24 reporter using Medi Lift twice daily for two weeks described a more defined chin and slightly raised cheeks, but found it painful and said the mask prevents drinking or brushing teeth.[1] This is one person's account.
